0.long_answer: H2 receptor antagonists, also known as H2 blockers, work by blocking the histamine H2 receptors on the stomach's parietal cells, which reduces the production of gastric acid. This mechanism is effective in lessening GERD symptoms by roughly 40%. Although they were once widely used for the treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease, their role has diminished with the advent of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), which offer more potent and longer-lasting acid suppression. Classic examples of H2 receptor antagonists include cimetidine, ranitidine, and famotidine.
